description: Biz ARGE Eğitimcileri ekibi olarak, eğitim teknolojileri ve yazılım geliştirme alanında yenilikçi çözümler üreten tutkulu bir ekibiz. NASA'nın açık verilerini kullanarak toplumsal fayda sağlayan, ölçeklenebilir ve akıllı projeler tasarlıyoruz. Ekibimizde yazılım geliştirme, arayüz tasarımı ve veri analizi konularında yetkin arkadaşlarımız bulunuyor. Aramıza katılacak yeni üyelerde problem çözme becerisi, yazılım/tasarım merakı ve takım çalışmasına yatkınlık arıyoruz. katılın!
summary: AERO-SHIELD is an AI-powered early warning system developed to detect potential fires in spacecraft and microgravity environments before smoke is generated. Due to the absence of rising hot gases in the space environment, fires can behave differently than on Earth, and conventional smoke detectors may perceive the danger late. As a solution to this problem, the system performs multi-sensor fusion by combining infrared temperature, oxygen, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and micro-particle data. The obtained data is analyzed using a special risk algorithm to calculate the probability of fire. If the risk level reaches a critical threshold, visual and audible alarms are generated, and an automatic isolation mechanism is designed to be activated. The working HTML/JavaScript prototype simulates different fire scenarios based on scientific findings obtained from NASA's FLEX, ACME, and Saffire experiments. AERO-SHIELD aims to enhance astronaut safety and enable earlier response to fires, particularly in Moon, Mars, and space station missions.
details:
On Earth, fire rises and smoke warns us; in space, flames burn like silent, spherical ghosts. AERO-SHIELD is an autonomous microgravity fire-prediction matrix that does not wait for smoke. To catch invisible cool flames (500–800 K) that blind conventional sensors, it fuses three independent physical signatures into a single real-time Risk Score (R): IR Thermal Heating (40%), Gas Gradients (O2 drop and CO/CO2 surge, 35%), and Laser Particulate Scattering (25%). At R >= 45, it alerts the crew; at R >= 75, it autonomously isolates cabin airflow to starve the fire before it spreads.
AERO-SHIELD delivers a 5x faster response by detecting solid-fuel fires in 11.6 seconds versus 63.6 seconds for legacy detectors. It also eliminates sensor blind spots by catching invisible cool flames and Kapton wire pyrolysis—completely missed by standard alarms—in just 16.2 seconds. This provides critical deep-space autonomy, protecting astronauts on Artemis, Lunar Gateway, and Mars missions where Earth-based help is days away.
Our breakthrough lies in abandoning Earth-centric convection models to engineer specifically for microgravity physics. All thresholds were calibrated against 30 TB of open NASA PSI datasets (Saffire, FLEX, ACME) and NASA-STD-3001 standards. Built on a zero-dependency, offline Edge JavaScript (Edge JS) architecture, the system executes decisions within seconds on low-power spacecraft nodes. Our team prioritized three critical factors: eliminating invisible-flame blind spots, preventing false alarms via weighted multi-sensor fusion, and guaranteeing ultra-fast offline execution under strict space hardware constraints.
